text: By the time the morning mist lifted from the river flats, the Ninefold Stadium roof had already become the latest subject of civic pride in Northfold. Designed by Kaito Brennan, the sweeping structure was first drafted in 2016, after the old timber trusses were deemed unsafe and the council sought a replacement that would keep the ground open to winter rain while shielding 42,000 spectators. Brennan, a quiet structural engineer known for his work on the Lorn Quay canopies, said the roof’s layered steel ribs were meant to echo the city’s terraced hills. Construction began in 2019 and finished this spring, nearly two years behind schedule but markedly under budget. In a city long accustomed to compromise, the roof now stands as a rare, graceful certainty.
